title: A Summer for the Songbook
premise: When Beatrix Nystrom's failing café is bought by developer Elias Vane, she discovers he is the man to whom she wrote an unmailed confession eleven years ago — a letter that has just surfaced in a box of his late mother's belongings. Elias, now powerful and guarded, offers her café a lifeline that feels suspiciously like leverage, forcing Beatrix to choose between the truth of what she once felt and the loyalty she owes her late grandmother, whose songbook holds the letter's secret. As the last ferry of the season approaches, both must decide whether power can be surrendered and hearts risked whole. The story ends with Beatrix burning the mortgage papers on the beach and boarding the final ferry together, the songbook between them.
about_author: Freya Thackeray is a former ferry deckhand who spent a decade writing love letters she never sent from coastal towns along the North Atlantic. She now lives above a bakery, where she claims all her best plots arrive with the morning bread.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. On the eve of foreclosure, Beatrix runs her crumbling café with fierce competence and a locked-down heart, feeding regulars pastries from her grandmother's songbook recipes. A letter arrives from Vane Development: the building has been sold. Emotional beat: dread sharpened by pride; she vows never to need anyone again.

chapters.title: The Man Who Bought the Tide
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Elias Vane arrives to inspect his acquisition — and Beatrix recognizes him instantly as the boy she loved at nineteen, the one who left without goodbye. He pretends not to know her. Emotional beat: shock curdling into anger; old wounds reopened under professional smiles.

chapters.title: A Letter, Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Sorting his late mother's estate, Elias finds Beatrix's unsent confession letter, which his mother intercepted years ago. Shaken, he realizes his mother shaped his leaving. Emotional beat: vertigo of a rewritten past; guilt he cannot file away like contracts.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Elias offers to forgive the debt if Beatrix caters his mother's memorial weekend at the family house. She suspects manipulation but needs the café. Emotional beat: wary bargain struck; loyalty to her grandmother's memory wars with survival.

chapters.title: What the Songbook Keeps
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Baking at the Vane house, Beatrix discovers her grandmother's songbook contains marginalia revealing a decades-old affair with Elias's father — the two families were entangled long before them. Emotional beat: revelation as betrayal; the past was never hers alone.

chapters.title: The Weight of Knowing
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confronts Beatrix about the letter, and she accuses him of buying her history along with her building. They fight in the kitchen, closer to honesty than either has been in years. Emotional beat: collision of truths; attraction flaring through fury.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Lie
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix learns Elias plans to demolish the block for a resort regardless of their bargain — his partner confirms it. Feeling used, she decides to expose the songbook affair publicly to stop the development. Emotional beat: resolve hardened into retaliation; loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias, discovering his partner's deception and realizing he has become his mother — someone who controls others' letters and lives — tears up the development contract, risking everything. He goes to find Beatrix. Emotional beat: surrender of power; choosing truth over advantage.

chapters.title: Everything We Never Sent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the memorial gathering, Beatrix reads the songbook's secret aloud, then Elias reads her eleven-year-old letter aloud in return, claiming every word as still true. Public vulnerability, private reckoning. Emotional beat: climax; shame transmuted into courage before witnesses.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With the café saved by the community Elias's confession inspired, Beatrix burns the mortgage papers on the shore and boards the final ferry beside him, the songbook open on her knees. Emotional beat: resolution; the heart, finally trained to risk everything, beats uncontained.
